finding: The live range of $130-$850 is too wide at the top; the bottom is about right. Our implied totals (plugs for all cylinders + hours x $120-$160 per hour, the national middle used for this arithmetic) are: economy 2015 Corolla 1.8L $109-$238; midsize 2017 CR-V 1.5L turbo $94-$272; truck 2016 F-150 5.0L V8 $160-$227; luxury 2013 BMW 335i $305-$469. Across the four, that is roughly $95-$470. At the bottom, our four-cylinder figures dip under $130 only because they pair the cheapest plug set with a manufacturer warranty time of 0.3-0.5 hours, which runs shorter than a shop bills; the outside estimates start at $100 (AAA, J.D. Power), $151 (Jerry) and $208 (YourMechanic), so $130 is a fair floor. At the top, nothing we could build and no outside estimate reaches $850: the dearest case we built is the six-cylinder BMW at $469 using a home mechanic's two-hour figure, RepairPal's all-vehicle average is $288-$399, AAA and J.D. Power top out near $500, and the highest shop/dealer comparison price seen was $574 for a late-model Corolla. A top of about $500-$600 fits these four vehicles. What we did not test: engines where the intake manifold has to come off to reach the rear plugs (many transverse V6s) and engines with more than eight plugs; Jerry says those layouts add about 0.5-1.5 hours, which would add roughly $60-$240 and could carry a dealer quote past $600. So $850 should be kept only as an explicit 'hard-to-reach engine' case, not as the normal top. Caveats on the labor times: no manufacturer or shop time was found for the Corolla itself, so its hours use a Honda warranty time for the same engine layout (low) and a repair-manual publisher's general 'up to an hour' (high); the CR-V high end is a do-it-yourself time for the 2.4L version of the same vehicle; the F-150 time is one seller's approximate 45 minutes; the BMW time is one do-it-yourself figure and a trained technician would likely be quicker, so the luxury total may be overstated. Caveats on parts: the per-plug prices on one retailer are listed as single plugs without the word 'each'; the NGK box for the CR-V was a sale price on an item marked sold out, and four Honda-boxed plugs at the discounted dealer price come to $89.96. The truck low changed from the earlier $84.99 store-brand set to $69.76 (eight Denso plugs) and the high is now the Ford list price.
extras: A quote often adds ignition coils or coil boots if any are cracked or oil-soaked, an intake manifold gasket on engines where the manifold has to come off to reach the rear plugs, a valve cover gasket if oil is found in the plug wells, a diagnosis fee if the visit started with a misfire or check engine light, shop supplies, and sales tax. Extra labor is common when a plug is seized or breaks during removal. The parts figures here are the plugs only.
